2.6.0.headline: A service's tests can be NUnit or xUnit, on one shared test infrastructure.
highlights: --TestFramework xunit generates a service's tests on xUnit v3; an integration test carries its category as the trait TestCategory, so CI selects it as it selects an NUnit category.

Common.Testing holds the test execution contexts, the PostgreSQL test databases, the stubs and the rule checks, with no test framework; Common.Tests and the services' tests reference it. TestSkip lets each test framework say how it skips a test.
Updating an earlier solution: a service's test project references Common.Testing instead of Common.Tests, and sets TestSkip.Handler; see upgrading.

2.5.0.headline: An audit journal of entity changes, published through the outbox, with guards for writes it cannot see.
highlights: --Audit with --Messaging outbox: an entity marked [Auditable] publishes AuditRecordedV1 for every change, in the same transaction, with the actor, the tenants, the diff and the correlation identifier; [AuditRedact] records a secret changing without its value.
IAuditRecorder and ISetBasedAuditCapture record writes past the change tracker; AuditBulkRecordedV1 carries the rows before and after.
A generated service runs four guards: every entity decided, markers valid, no secret in the journal, every set-based write declared with [SetBasedWrite].

2.4.0.headline: Tokens in HttpOnly cookies with CSRF protection, set by the deployment instead of guessed.
highlights: AuthCookies:SameSite and AuthCookies:ServedOverHttps state the deployment; SameSite=None without HTTPS, or with any CORS origin and credentials, refuses to start with what to change.

With AuthCookies:RequireCsrfHeader, a POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE a token cookie would authenticate needs the X-CSRF header, or is refused with 403 CSRF_HEADER_MISSING; Authorization headers and API keys are not checked.
IssueTokenCookies, ReadRefreshTokenCookie and ClearTokenCookies cover login, refresh and logout; a rule test in a generated service fails when a response carries a token.
A service generated now has the section with Lax and the check on. Without it, as in an earlier solution, cookies behave as before; add the section once the frontend sends the header.

2.3.0.headline: A secret store outage is survivable, and one feature flag can be changed during it.
highlights: Infisical__SnapshotPath: every successful read of the secret store is copied to a file only its owner can read, and a start that cannot reach the store runs on that copy, with a warning. Off by default, because the copy holds the secrets.

"pinned": true on a flag in features.json makes the file decide it, over the store, its snapshot and environment variables; such flags report the source Pinned, and every start names them in a warning.
Only the file can pin a flag, so the store cannot lock its own values in.

2.2.0.headline: Commands a client may repeat run once per key.
highlights: IIdempotentExecutor: the first request with a key does the work and records its answer in the same transaction; a repeat gets that answer. Two requests racing with one key create one thing, decided by a unique index.
A key reused for another operation, a failed attempt, an answer that must not be stored and a duplicate the work itself refuses each get their own outcome; see persistence.
Opt in per service: modelBuilder.AddIdempotencyLog() and services.AddIdempotency<TContext>(). Tested on PostgreSQL.

2.1.3.headline: Images are named after the product too, so two solutions on one host keep their own.
highlights: Fixed: an image was named <REGISTRY>/<service>, and two solutions with an Orders service on one host built and ran each other's image; it is now <REGISTRY>/<product>-<service>.

deploy/build-images.sh reads each service's image name from its deploy files, so a service generated by an earlier version keeps its name. In a solution generated earlier, take the new build-images.sh before generating a service with this version.

2.1.2.headline: Blue-green keeps the serving color serving when a deploy fails.
highlights: Fixed: when the edge did not answer after the switch, bluegreen.sh exited with the edge left on the new color; it now points the edge back at the previous one.
Fixed: an infrastructure container recreated during up, by a changed setting or image, left the running color without its database; both colors are reconnected.
A color that does not become ready is stopped and its last log lines printed; the active color is not touched.
One bluegreen.sh run at a time; a lock left by a killed run is taken over.

2.1.1.headline: Services are added to All.sln without a terminal too.
highlights: Fixed: src/services/manual-add-projects.sh failed with exit code 1 when run without a terminal, as in CI, on the pause it kept for a window opened by a double click.

2.1.0.headline: Deployment, an API gateway, CI and one correlation identifier end to end; compatible with 2.0.
highlights: Every dependency - the database, Hangfire, RabbitMQ - can be switched off in configuration; a service without its database starts, and what needs the database answers 503.
--Deploy generates docker compose or Kubernetes files; under compose a blue-green switch with rollback that needs no rebuild.
--ApiGateway generates a YARP gateway that validates the token once and passes the user and permissions to the services with the internal key.
--Storage adds S3-compatible object storage, with SeaweedFS under compose; --ClickHouse adds connections, a schema check at startup and readiness.
--GitHubCiCd adds CI: build, unit and integration tests on real servers, coverage with a branch threshold, and a secret scan of incoming commits.
One correlation identifier across HTTP, the message bus, Hangfire jobs and calls to other services; AddInternalServiceHandlers() makes any HTTP client a call to another service of the product.

Common: a system execution context for jobs and consumers, readable numbers from a PostgreSQL sequence, text normalised before validation, accepted string values in the API schema, the client's scheme and address behind a proxy.
Integration tests run on a PostgreSQL database of their own, cloned from one migrated template; a generated service has a test that its container is complete.
Fixed: replicas starting together no longer race to create the schema.

2.0.0.headline: A layered microservice solution with a shared web host, three-phase domain events and opt-in infrastructure.
highlights: Each service is Domain, Application, Infrastructure and API; a project sees only the projects it references itself.
One web host from Common.Web: logging, JSON, CORS, Swagger, validation and the pipeline, with the DI container validated at startup.
Errors are RFC 9457 problems carrying the correlation identifier; failed validation answers 422.
Domain events run in three phases tied to the transaction - before save, after commit, on rollback - and reach Hangfire jobs.
Permissions are declared on actions and checked from the token's claims; services accept a JWT and the internal API key.
Each service owns a PostgreSQL schema, checked at startup; repositories take queries as specifications.
Opt-in by flag: Hangfire, MassTransit with a transactional outbox, secrets from Infisical, feature flags, an API contract diff on pull requests, access rules over a tenant tree.
Package versions in one Directory.Packages.props, the product version by hand in version.json; /health and /ready report the version and the commit.
One Dockerfile builds every service.

1.0.0.headline: The template before the breaking changes of 2026.
